sources.entry: AudioSync - Play your Mac's audio on AirPlay, Google Cast and local speakers at once, in sync. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/yassersutojoyo/audiosync) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that plays your Mac's audio on AirPlay, Google Cast and local speakers at once, delaying local speakers so everything stays in sync.
summary.what_it_does: AudioSync captures the Mac's system audio, one app's audio, or an input device (mic or audio interface) and sends it to AirPlay speakers, Apple TVs, Google Cast speakers, and any output macOS can play to (built-in, headphone jack, HDMI, USB, Bluetooth). Local speakers each get an adjustable delay from -2 to +20 seconds, plus a separate AirPlay delay, to line them up with AirPlay's roughly two-second lag. It offers per-speaker and master volume, a 10-band EQ, zones that switch together with their own volume, and auto-connect, launch at login, and Now Playing for Spotify and Music on the Mac. Newer releases add calibration with a microphone, presets, and a Web Remote that lets a phone on the home network control speakers. Google Cast speakers are synced by a manually set offset rather than automatically. A Windows 11 preview and a Linux preview (not yet released) are also described.
use_cases: Play Mac audio on AirPlay and local speakers in sync
Multiroom music around the house from a Mac
Remove echo when the same song plays on AirPlay and local speakers
Stream Mac sound to Google Cast speakers
Calibrate speaker delays with a microphone
Control speakers from a phone on the home network
how_to_run: Download AudioSync.dmg from the latest release on the Releases page
Open the disk image and drag AudioSync to Applications (requires macOS 15 or later)
On first launch, approve the app in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway
Or from Terminal: curl -fsSL <script URL> | bash (downloads the latest release, checks SHA-256, installs and opens it)
Grant Screen & System Audio Recording, Local Network, and optionally Microphone and Automation permissions
Pick a source, then click a speaker's round icon to turn it on
notable: Delays local speakers so they line up with AirPlay's roughly two-second lag
Calibrate with Microphone measures a local speaker's delay automatically
Zones switch speakers on and off together, each with its own volume
Web Remote lets a phone on the home network control the app (plain HTTP)
Windows and Linux builds share the same Rust engine as the Mac app
caveats: Everything AirPlay-side runs about two seconds late, which is poor for video and games
AirPlay 2 is experimental and off by default; Google Cast needs manual offsets and can drift, with Resync causing a short gap
Several Bluetooth outputs at once may stutter, and the app is not notarized so the first launch needs an extra approval step
keywords: play same song on every speaker
